scenario_text: An enzyme is studied in the presence of an inhibitor that binds the same site as the substrate. Independent assays vary both the substrate level and the inhibitor level, and the instantaneous velocity is recorded. Increasing inhibitor raises the apparent substrate requirement while leaving the maximal velocity unchanged. Each measurement uses a freshly prepared, independent condition.

derivation_notes: At high substrate concentration a second substrate molecule can bind the ES complex nonproductively, so mass-action on this dead-end complex adds an S**2/Ksi term in the denominator, causing velocity to decline past an optimal S.
change_summary: Relaxed the single-substrate-binding assumption to allow nonproductive binding of a second substrate to ES (substrate inhibition), adding the S**2/Ksi denominator term while preserving all competitive-inhibition structure.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Only one substrate molecule binds the active site, so velocity rises monotonically to Vmax with increasing S.
assumption_audit.mechanism: A second substrate molecule can bind the enzyme-substrate complex to form a catalytically inactive ternary complex; including this dead-end equilibrium refines the high-substrate regime and produces the characteristic decline in velocity at excess substrate.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: As Ksi -> infinity the S**2/Ksi term vanishes and the equation returns exactly to the parent competitive-inhibition form.

derivation_notes: The inhibitor is assumed to bind only the free enzyme (purely competitive), but a nominally competitive inhibitor that occupies the active site can retain weak affinity for the enzyme-substrate complex, producing a mixed-inhibition term. Adding the ES-I equilibrium (governed by Kis) introduces an S*I cross term in the denominator, reducing to pure competitive inhibition as Kis becomes large.
change_summary: Relaxed the strictly competitive assumption on I by allowing the inhibitor to also bind the ES complex with dissociation constant Kis, turning the model into a mixed-inhibition scheme while preserving all existing mechanisms.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The inhibitor binds exclusively to the free enzyme (purely competitive), so no enzyme-substrate-inhibitor ternary complex forms.
assumption_audit.mechanism: An active-site-directed inhibitor can retain residual affinity for the ES complex; including the ES-I ternary equilibrium adds an S*I cross term (Km*I*S/(Ki*Kis)) to the denominator, converting pure competitive inhibition into mixed inhibition.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: As Kis -> infinity the new S*I cross term vanishes and the equation reverts exactly to the parent purely competitive form.
